sources.title: RIT CSCI-603 Computational Problem Solving catalog description
sources.author: Rochester Institute of Technology
sources.content: This course focuses on the application of computational thinking using a problem-centered approach. Specific topics include: expression of algorithms in pseudo-code and a programming language; elementary data structures such as lists, trees and graphs; problem solving using recursion; and debugging and testing. Assignments (both in class and homework) requiring a pseudo-code solution and implementation in a programming language are an integral part of the course. Note: This course serves as a bridge course for graduate students and cannot be taken by undergraduate students without permission from the CS Undergraduate Program Coordinator. This course is restricted to students in COMPSCI-MS. Contact Hours: Lecture 3 Typically Offered: Fall, Spring

sources.title: Python Language Reference
sources.author: Python Software Foundation
sources.content: The Python language reference specifies lexical analysis, data model behavior, execution, expressions, statements, functions, classes, exceptions, and module import semantics. Python objects have identity, a type, and a value. Names are bound to objects within namespaces and scopes. Expressions produce values, while statements control execution and bindings. Exceptions interrupt normal control flow until a matching handler processes them or they propagate. The import system searches for modules and binds loaded modules into a namespace. Programs should be reasoned about through explicit state, control flow, data representation, contracts, tests, and observable behavior. Debugging separates syntax, runtime, and logical failures, while decomposition and abstraction reduce the number of interacting concerns.

sources.title: LLVM Language Reference Manual
sources.author: LLVM Project
sources.content: LLVM IR is a typed, SSA-based intermediate representation with explicit instructions, basic blocks, functions, memory operations, and control flow. A module contains global values, functions, declarations, and metadata. A function contains basic blocks, and every basic block ends with a terminator instruction. Phi instructions select values according to the predecessor control-flow edge. Load and store instructions make memory access explicit. Valid IR must satisfy structural and typing rules. The verifier reports IR that violates those rules. Compiler work separates parsing and semantic analysis from lowering, verification, optimization, and target-specific code generation.
